rule.title: Ban on coordinated pricing algorithms for rents
rule.requirement: It is illegal to sell rent-setting algorithms that use private competitor data to Berkeley landlords, and illegal for landlords to use them to set rents or occupancy levels. Each month and each unit is a separate violation.
rule.requirement_es: Es ilegal vender a los propietarios de Berkeley algoritmos que usan datos privados de competidores para fijar rentas, y es ilegal que los propietarios los usen para fijar rentas o niveles de ocupación. Cada mes y cada unidad cuenta como una violación separada.
rule.key_value: Up to $1,000 civil penalty per violation
rule.coverage_text: Residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley. Covers any process using nonpublic competitor data (less than 90 days old) to recommend rents, fees, occupancy or lease terms; excludes aggregated anonymous reports, affordable-housing rent/income limit tools, and market research, appraisal, or software development uses.
rule.penalty: City Attorney may sue for damages, injunctive relief, restitution and civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; aggrieved tenants may sue for injunctive relief, damages and civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation, plus attorney's fees.
rule.quote:
B. It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley.
